working: Traffic more than doubled month over month: 1,158 sessions in the last 30 days (07-21 to 08-19) vs 553 in the prior 30 (+109%), and the 1,100-day window now totals 32,529 sessions.
Organic Search grew 39.1% period over period (225 -> 313 sessions) and holds 33.1% of the full window (10,772 of 32,529), keeping SEO the strongest earned channel.

GSC over the trailing 30 days shows 4,126 impressions, 53 clicks and an impression-weighted average position of 14.19 across 90 pages - a real presence to convert, since most of those pages sit just off page one.

The Alumni list remains the healthiest audience on file: Alumni eNews - July 2026 (07-09) posted a 57.3% open on 1,028 sends with +77.2% session lift, and the 07-16 reminder held 46.77% open with the best recent click rate at 1.06%.
Open rates are not the problem anywhere: 51.62% average across all 100 tracked campaigns and 47.0% across the 29 sends in 2026, both far above the 25-35% health/nonprofit benchmark.
not_working: No newsletter has gone out in 31 days. The most recent send is 2026-07-20 (Staff-Client eNews - July 2026 and Referring Partners eNews - July 2026); the list has been idle through the entire traffic surge.

UTM leakage remains total. Across all 29 sends in 2026, GA4 credits just 12 Email sessions in the 3 days after a send against 1,255 Direct sessions - newsletter links carry no utm_source/utm_medium, so GA4 files every click under Direct. Email is 20 of 32,529 window sessions (0.1%) while Direct is 51.3%.

The Constant Contact OAuth client is still broken: the live refresh failed again with 401 invalid_client. The dashboard is running on cached campaign data that ends at the 07-20 send, so open/click figures will silently go stale.

Both July 20 sends landed flat-to-negative: Staff-Client eNews - July 2026 (8,906 sends, 47.93% open) and Referring Partners eNews - July 2026 (958 sends, 27.35% open) both sat on a -27.3% session lift. Referring Partners has now opened at 26-27% for two straight months, below benchmark.
Click rates are weak list-wide: 1.18% average across 2026 sends versus 1.94% lifetime, and 14 of the 29 2026 sends produced negative session lift.
Organic Social fell 22.6% period over period (31 -> 24 sessions) and is only 5.3% of the window - the smallest contribution of any owned channel BCC actively works.
do_next: Fix the Constant Contact OAuth client secret first (see CONSTANT-CONTACT-SETUP.md). Everything email-side is now frozen at 07-20 and each additional send goes unmeasured.

Tag every link in the next send with ?utm_source=constantcontact&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=<send-name>. Until that ships, all newsletter credit keeps landing in Direct and email ROI cannot be argued.
Restart the cadence - the August Alumni and Staff-Client sends are overdue by a month. Alumni is the highest-yield list on record (57.3% open, +77.2% lift in July).
Send Tuesday or Wednesday, not Monday/Thursday/weekend: 2026 sends average +40.6% lift on Tuesday and +27.4% on Wednesday versus -2.0% Monday, -3.8% Thursday and -32.2% Saturday.

Repromote event-driven content - it is the only theme that has ever driven real clicks (Client eNews December(2) at 10.17% click / 19.35% click-to-open; 2024 Alumni Events November at 4.80% click, +64.7% lift).
Work the near-page-one SEO pages: with average position 14.19 and 4,126 impressions against only 53 clicks, title/meta rewrites on the top impression pages are the cheapest click gain available.
Audit the Direct spike (209 -> 735 sessions, +251.7%) with no newsletter sent in that window - confirm it is real demand and not bot or referral-stripped traffic before crediting it to marketing.
summary: Site traffic more than doubled month over month to 1,158 sessions, led by a +251.7% Direct surge and +39.1% Organic Search, but the newsletter program has been dark for 31 days and the Constant Contact OAuth client is still returning 401 invalid_client. The single highest-value fix stays the same: repair the CC connection and add UTM tags, because GA4 currently credits 1,255 post-send Direct sessions against just 12 Email sessions across all of 2026.
